title: AI Map generation (puzzle)
author: Substantial_Fish6717
selftext:
I am working on a 'Cup Heroes' alike game. Game looks amazing, but I am having trouble with the map generation (the little puzzle where the player decides where each ball will go and usually aim for their larger multipliers)

the maps that the ai generates are usually very random with things that look very out of place  and sometimes with some multipliers being unreachable. what do you guys use for this kind of scenario?

comments.author: Moist_Signal_5080
comments.body: I havent had any success with 2D or 3D map designs with AI, it always seems very random and makes no sense. I just have it make me something so I can go in and design the maps myself.

replies.author: Substantial_Fish6717
replies.body: I have literally just edited the post to add that i am going to do that manually as a last resort, so I think we are on the same situation

comments.author: AccomplishedPie9339
comments.body:
Try to set rules for a map being generated: important zones reachability, expected player’s path etc. 

I haven’t played cup heroes, but I believe that generalized approach would be pretty similar: you don’t want the AI to generate game level from scratch,   you better generate some sort of a framework for this generation with constraints: some mechanics, supposed intent, danger zones. Then you can build auto tests to check if the generated level is at least passable and after that review manually the final outcome

replies.author: work_in_marketing
replies.body: I kinda did this last week just by telling Claude to cluster terrain of the same type. I'm sure you can continue with that and write very elaborate rules. Or you could probably just ask it to research on how others do it, learn from it, and then apply what you believe would give the best result.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Use AI to build a level generator, don't ask AI to generate the levels.

replies.author: Substantial_Fish6717
replies.body: Yeah I think this is the answer. I already have the assets that I generated with Codex/Meshy/Blender. So I can just ask the AI to build a visual generator where I can drag and drop the assets I want, where I want them.. Not a bad idea at all, I'll definitely try this one
